Lemma
[smooth curves have integrable speed and energy density]

↗ def:dc-ch9-2-2-energy

1. ch9:2.2If a curve is smooth on an open neighborhood of $[a,b]$, then its speed and squared speed are continuous there and integrable on $[a,b]$. Consequently its arc length and energy on $[a,b]$ are represented by ordinary interval integrals.
Proof

\sketch Near each time, choose one coordinate chart containing the curve. In that chart the velocity depends continuously on time, and the metric coefficients are smooth, so the squared speed is continuous. Its nonnegative square root is the speed and is also continuous. Continuous functions on the compact interval $[a,b]$ are integrable.

□
